newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mazda to launch sport vehicle next year--sources.
newsitem.headline: Mazda to launch sport vehicle next year--sources.

text.p: Mazda Motor Corp is expected to launch a sport-utility vehicle next year, based on its CUX concept car which was unveiled at the 1995 Tokyo Motor Show, industry sources said on Wednesday.
The nation's fifth-ranked automaker has lagged behind rivals Honda Motor Co Ltd and Toyota Motor Corp in developing compact recreational vehicles, they said.
A Mazda spokeswoman declined to comment. "We cannot make any comment about our future products," she said.

But Mazda president Henry Wallace told reporters last Friday that Mazda was trying to increase production at its Hofu plant in western Japan, and in order to do so it would start producing a new model at the plant next year. But he did not say what type of vehicle that would be.
Earlier on Wednesday, Kyodo news agency quoted company officials as saying Mazda would launch a 1.6-litre five-door sport-utility model based on the CUX concept car.
Mazda, owned 33.4 percent by Ford Motor Co, also plans to add yet another sport-utility vehicle in 1999 to its lineup, which will be larger than the planned 1.6-litre model, Kyodo reported.
